item.title: Surrey Women's Cross Country League Division 1, Race 4, Denbies Vineyard, Dorking
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Engine Room Swings Into Gear

Will Cockerell reports:- This was a gung-ho tribe that rounded off our campaign and we were pleased to welcome two new names to our all-time list of Surrey League scorers. After that incredible start by Thames back in October, the league title always seemed just out of reach, and after sniffing about the possibility of dragging Sammi and Tish to the course in shackles [they ran 78 and 79 at Wokingham], and parachuting in Lou from Cheshire, we still felt it wouldn't have quite been enough. Maybe we could have scored 55 points and hope for a miracle? We'd still have been 3 pips short!

So instead this was a day for our engine-room to come to the party - the backbone and foundation of any successful club - and they excelled themselves. After Fee's metronomic sequence of finishes for the season of 16, 18, 21 & 19, Jojo turned in another peach, whilst Vix is flying at the mo, up from 58th to 45th on a month ago. Laura had even more of a stunner and turned her Nonsuch 90th into 58th, while Maisie's 101 on debut is now 88th. Finally, welcome to Belgrave 'Run and Become' employee Petra Kasperova. Petra kept tabs on Laura all through to indicate she will be a useful ally in the years to come.

It was exciting to watch Dulwich's assault on Thames for the title. It was touch and go, and a clerical error initially awarded the spoils the Dulwich, but instead it was Thames who claimed the trophy by a mere 17 points. How well we did to scalp them in two out of four events, and we look forward to another exciting scrap next season. With Herne Hill and West 4 also on the rise, and SLH always solid, it could be a six-way battle for supremacy. Many thanks to the 16 runners who fought so hard for us this term - 3rd place in such a strong league is honourable.

A foot injury slowed Yasmin down a bit in the Under 13 age group but she courageously kept going ... and then went up to Farthing Downs to watch Paskar in action.

item.title: SEAA CC Champs, Parliament Hill Fields
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
"Little dog!"

Alan Mead writes:- Starting half-way up the hill instead of down at the Lido was a slight relief but there was still 50 minutes of running ahead of our stalwarts who come together each year to celebrate the toughest cross country race in our calendar. The postponement from three weeks earlier, due to the Heath being snowbound, resulted in a few of our men being unable to turn out; overall the field was down about 40% but the team race was hit hard.

Paskar and Andrew Connick were both prominent as the field went over the top and round the back of Kite Hill for the first time but already it was Frank Tickner of Wells City and Bedford’s Neilson Hall slugging it out for the lead. A lap later, with both our men in the ‘teens and the mud spattering up to eye level, it was Andrew putting our Vice-Captain under a pressure he hasn’t faced all winter – a club-mate showing every sign of getting away from him. Will Cockerell and Matt Taylor (what a boost he has given our team this winter) were similarly locked together and with Mike Trees and Roy Maddams completing the six and John Needham and Tom Hadfield backing up, we showed every sign of finishing a squad in a reasonable position. Bedford & County had the team race stitched up by a long way.

As Mike headed out again he was overtaken by a barking pooch that was having the time of his life. Following the flags over hill and dale he cheerfully barked and looked up at every runner he overtook with a sort of doggy grin: “Come on, hang on to me, we can catch ‘em.” Eight or nine minutes later our friend had worked his way further up the field, still going well, and as the racers came towards the end of lap two he’d caught Will and was by now drawing as much support as the runners: “Come on Will, come on Matt, come on dog!” Our own team manager was all for slipping a Belgrave vest on him but the course police arrested said canine, now intent on making an assault on the leaders, before he could set out on lap three.

Stitch caused Andrew a few problems over the second half of the race but his was a brilliant run. What a way to celebrate his birthday. Paskar was less than happy in the mud and Matt Taylor eventually got the better of the Cockerpillar. They don’t come any tougher than Mike Trees – an M50 and having just driven down from Northumberland to race, was going back again that night – what a hero. Sixth as a squad was not bad at all.

And our headline? An expression used by H.G.Wells’ Mr Polly whenever he found himself in a sticky situation and similarly used by your correspondent on occasions when a swift exit has been required.

item.title: ECCA National CC Championships, Herrington Country Park, Sunderland
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
The National's Glorious Ebb and Flow

Will Cockerell writes: - The Belles' 2012-13 cross-country campaign ended with this interesting little scamper under the Penshaw Monument folly. To the uninitiated, there was plenty more folly going on down below, but for some reason, the craziness of the day makes sense to a good portion of the 3,000+ participants, as much as paint-balling, cheese-rolling or dwarf tossing does to others.
To be sure, the logistics don't seem to jive. A 16-17-hour round trip for 30-40 minutes of the most gluey, gloopy, freezing, ghoulish conditions one ever did see. 2007 this was not, when Frank Tickner shimmied round the park in 37:31. Keith Gerrard needed more than 30-seconds-per-mile to take care of the distance - and this correspondent 41.

At around 0630hrs Sammi, Tish & Ma, Laura, Hester and the 'pillar popped their heads out from their burrows, and started out on the fiddly journey to King's Cross. Loading up on caffeine, they were then smoothly ferried up to Sunderland grimly noting that England's green and pleasant land started to turn white at around York (aided and abetted by a snowstorm). They were greeted at Sunderland by the aptly named Lou Blizzard, a key scorer in the best National performance in our history in 2005 [12th]. A seven-seater cab whisked us up to Herrington (and how nice to see the park's namesake, Chaz, in the crowd - our 15th most 'blinged' relay-runner this century and key National cross man in our Stowe and Bristol campaigns of 2000 and '02).

It didn't take much to see that the battlefield before us was not for the faint-hearted. Mud splattered athletes from the age-groups walked around like zombies, long since having lost feeling in their extremities. Half-an-hour before the gun and SA's feet were frozen blocks which given her other niggles was always going to make running at optimum pace a problem. For a moment there was concern that she would DNS, but announced: "I haven't come all this way for nothing." A final photo op with JK before the off, who was pastiche-interviewed about the Belles' prospects: "Think this lot can go top 6, Jim?" "Well looking at them they seem very mean, lean and hungry, so they must have a chance." Profound.

Early doors and it was clear Lou had a big problem. She had stepped in a hole the week before and her ankle had blown up to twice the size. Surely the National was out, but she wouldn't let it go, and after nailing the Wrexham Half declared herself fit. But suspect ankles were like a match to a scarecrow on this course, and Lou was in for a whole world of pain. That she stuck it out was a marvel - a true Belgrave hero.

But we had back-up, and Jojo was suddenly under the spotlight, and didn't she grab it with glee, nearly scoring 2nd for us as it went, as she placed Fee behind her for the first time. Fee was 17 pips up on her excellent National of last year, and yet again was the backbone of our operation. We are so grateful to the 'Maycock massive' for all the support they've given us these last two years, and particular menche should go to Drew and Finlay, who are uncomplaining, often hypothermic, and on this occasion clad in footwear more appropriate for Ibiza.

Laura had a cracker to go way inside the top half, whilst our 'sweeper' HBR bashed out the 'stat' of the day, as she turned her 302 last year into 145. Which only leaves our 'two-headed monster', who have catapulted us into the limelight this season. Sam toiled in the gloop and never gave up, and the roads will feel so easy after this. We know given fairer conditions this is a very fine cross-country runner - Brighton '12 - proved that, but this was about getting the job done, when she could instead have imploded.

If we thought Tish was exceptional last week, this was truly stunning. Her 1:35 defeat to Steph Twell in London became a mere 12 seconds here, as it just shows that no-one, no matter their class and experience, was exempt from turmoil if things started to go awry. As for Tish, despite struggling to control her nerves, she executed her race dead centre, and typically for her, still craved more. That 'more' will come race-by-race, as she is steadily climbs up the ranks of England's foremost endurance runners.

So, scores at the doors? We got that top 6, with the next three clubs neatly lined up bang in front of us - ooh, what could have been with a bit more luck. But they'll all say the same - Hallamshire for instance lost Hattie Dean the week before - so no ifs, no buts, this is where we currently belong in the nation's pecking order. Some logistical acrobatics were required, but well worth all the effort and expense. This team is perfectly poised for many more top-sixes over the coming generation - bring it on.

A magnificent 25th place came from James Kelly in the men's race. "I died a thousand deaths over the last kilometre," he later admitted, "Bring on the 12 stage." Sadly we were unable to get a full team together and as a result several of those who had planned to run baulked at a round trip of 600 miles to run in an incomplete team. Malik Nehaili showed his love of the sport by combining a run in the under 13 Boys event while on a few days break in the North East.

item.title: ERRA Women's National 6-Stage Road Relay, Sutton Coldfield
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Belles just out of the medals


President and Team Manager Charlie Dickinson, Rose O'Brien, Tish Jones, Jo Rhodes, Fee Maycock, Alison Heydenrych, Sam Amend, Louise Blizzard and Vikki Goodwin.

Charlie Dickinson writes:- A very strong team came to Sutton Park with just a hope of getting one of the minor South of England medals, given out because of the Milton Keynes cancellation three weeks ago. After a wonderful performance from everyone, the team were left disappointed just 12 seconds short of the bronze.

What a wonderful group of girls we have, the Magnificent 8. All arrived early, warmed up themselves without being reminded, reported to the changeover in good time, supported and encouraged each other, and ran their hearts out, a Team Manager’s Dream!
Jojo ran the first leg to order. Not phased by the fast mass start and top loading teams, she kept to her own pace finishing strongly just as predicted. Rose on leg two, a 400m track girl, but with an excellent ‘Bridges’ a week ago, kept to a sensible steady pace up to the memorial, but just as she was set to unleash that track speed down the hill, she was crippled with severe stitch and had to ease off right at the wrong time. She still finished strongly to complete in a very satisfactory time but was left very frustrated hoping low 18's.

Louise has been troubled by a badly swollen ankle and worried that she would let the team down after missing a great deal of training. She did nothing of the sort running a typically gutsy third leg pulling back three places. Then to Tish on leg 4. She ran just as we have come to expect from our new superstar. Flying round in 16:51 she moved us up from 27th to 14th and getting just about in sight of those medals.
Sammi on the difficult leg five has herself been nursing and ignoring her Achilles injury prior to the marathon next week. We can always count on Sammi to pull out a great performance and this was no exception. With large gaps to chase down she moved us up one more place to 13th.

The always dependable Fee was trusted with the final leg and she ran a blinder and in now difficult windy conditions a mere one second from her time last year. Storming past the girl from Norwich just 30 meters from the finish was typical of how she has run all season.
Then the long wait for the results, were the South not giving the silver to Aldershot ‘B’ whose ‘A’ team had got the gold miles in front? We were ahead of Norwich, did that make us third? But no, we had overlooked the runner from Bedford running 17.35 on the last leg to pip us by an agonising 12 seconds.

If only! The stitch, the ankle, the Achilles, all finding just another two seconds each! But that's how we all are, never happy always wanting more, and all determined to come back next year and get that medal!
But we were not done yet, up to the top of the hill to egg on the men's team and to see our Will stick to the Leeds man like glue and not let him get away. And so pleased for him to get that gold medal after all he has done for the women's team.
A final huge thank you to Vicky and Alison who came as reserves, never complained and were truly just as much part of the team. Alison ran a blinder on leg two and showed that if it had been seven legs we would have certainly got that medal!

item.title: Southern Athletics League Division 3 (S), Match 1, Hastings
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Not a bad turn-out in sunny if somewhat windy conditions. A happy band had travelled down in the mini-bus driven by Don Anderson but Triathlon superstar Richard Stannard cycled the 70 miles to Hastings to run in the 5000m. That race was won by Matt Graham who was unchallenged after throwing in a 69 second first lap. Not a single point was dropped in the men's throws - great work by Chris Privett and Pete Mayfield. 800 metre winner James Myatt found out that he could triple jump by handsomely winning that event and also enjoyed himself by tackling the high jump, 1500m and 4x400m where he looked every inch a one lap racer.

Biggest points scorer for Belgrave among the women's events was hammer thrower Rachel Basford who won that and took in the other throws, long jump and hurdles before finishing off with the relays. Team Manager Hazel Mead made it a hammer double by winning the B event in a near personal best. Jessica Case won the B 400 hurdles while Rose O'Brien and Sandra Dike seemed to pop up all over the arena.

With a few more of those blank spaces on the team sheet filled we can start challenging for a team win.

Nice to see Bob Bridges back with the team.

item.title: UK Women's Athletics League Division 3, Match 1, Leeds
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Great result from match 1 at Leeds

With athletes dropping out through injuries we took a team of just nine to the John Charles Stadium and team manager Bob Bridges thought it would be a damage limitation exercise; but the nine performed magnificently and if we can fill some of the blank spaces (as per normal the 1500m and upwards) we could be in danger of promotion. As Bob said afterwards, "It is days like this that makes it all worthwhile".

item.title: Club Clothing
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Greg's Blog

Thursday 25 April

First run over! Unfortunately it wasn't the result I was hoping for with training going the way it is, but I learnt a lot from the experience. The meet wasn't particularly well organised and me and my training partner had to end our warm ups prematurely to make our race! Never happened before but I now know how I'll deal with that situation in the future. So the 100 turned out to be a very rushed and panicky run where neither of us executed the skills we've been learning this winter. The time in the end was 10.53 which, upon reflection, was an ok opener. The 200 was another learnt lesson, don't try and sprint the whole thing flat out! I came off the bend well in the lead then, inevitably, died.

Next run is this Saturday which will just be a 100. Goals for this one are simply to execute the race well. I had my last track session today (Thursday) before it and have posted some promising times. So I'll be hoping for a faster run and just keep chopping my time down as I move into the season and approach the trials.

Next update will be the second race!

Photos are of me and some of the others at the track on a bit of a gloomy day and the morning view from our apartment!

Monday 15 April 2013

This week has been a fairly standard week of training. Lots of hard work and some very unpredictable weather. The track we're based at is quite a hard mondo surface so we've had to look for alternative places to train as everyone's bodies are beginning to hurt! The week coming will be the last block of training for this phase as we approach race season.

I'll be opening my season this Saturday the 20th in the 100m and 200m at the Tom Jones Memorial meet in Gainesville, Florida. It'll be an assessment of where I'm at with training at the moment as we're being peaked for July (trials time). I had a slight pull in my hamstring last week but it seems to have been dealt with and I'm really excited to see what ill run on the weekend. As we're still in quite heavy volume training wise, it takes the pressure and expectation off the first meet and I can just look forward to competing and racing. Everyone in the group is training well and most will be opening their own season this weekend too.

Stay tuned for season opener updates!

Picture: Team Christie in Orlando

Back row clockwise from left: Ryan Scott, Me, Dannish Walker-Khan, Aisha Naibe-Way, Linford, Richard Strachan, Ricardo Dos Santos Soares, Nigel Levine, Funsho Joseph, Conrad Williams.

Front row: Byron Robinson, Luke Lennon-Ford, Margaret Adeoye, Nicola Hill, Nicole Macdermott.

Tuesday 9 April 2013

Hello Belgravians!

For those who don't know me, I'm Greg Cackett and I run the 100m and 200m. I'm coached by Linford Christie and for the next four weeks I'm living the hard life in Daytona Beach, Florida. I'm training hard for what I hope will be a successful summer season. This is my first experience of warm weather training so Bill, Alan and I thought it might be interesting to do a few little posts to describe my experiences on this trip; hopefully you'll agree!

I've just finished my first week out here and, while the jet lag took some getting over, the main thing I've had to get used to is the sun on my poor pale skin! Sunburn aside though, running in the heat makes such a difference. You feel you can run fast without the worry of cold muscles cramping or pulling. I've been lucky enough as well to have received sound advice from Mr Laws on the dangers of getting too carried away in the heat. With that in mind I've been working myself hard but doing my best to stay healthy at the same time. Treatment from my training partner and masseur Richard Strachan, plus extra stretching is keeping the niggles at bay. We had a little trip to Orlando too, trained at the Disney track and I managed to pick up some new Puma gear so, for a couple of days at least, I'm not the team scruff-ball!

All in all it's been hard work but a lot of fun and I'm looking forward to what the next few weeks are going to bring and describing to you all an experience I feel lucky to be a part of. A short while ago I was playing Saturday league football with my mates and now I'm on a warm weather training camp with Linford Christie and a squad of international athletes. It's been a mad couple of years.

Thanks for reading and all the best for your summer seasons.

Restored from the club's earlier website, belgraveharriers.com, and published here as originally written.

item.title: Young Belgravians' Results 2013
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
By Will Cockerell

After the numerous excitement and varied glories of 2011-12, we came into this term with high expectations, and little did we know that the season would be underpinned by one of the greatest signings in our history.

We started off with an enjoyable day at the Surrey relays where Genia, Alison, Rieko and Catherine propelled us to do a tidy 5th; but then a week later: fireworks! On a glorious Indian summer's day we completed no fewer than three teams at the SEAA 6 stage road relay and our A team came away with the most thrilling of bronze medals as Runa Bostad, sister of Anne Hegvold, took us onto the podium inside the last 100 yards, with an almighty kick from around a quarter of a mile out. Only Aldershot had the better of us, with their B team 13 seconds away in silver. It was also the day that we unleashed the best kept secret in town on the UK club athletics sisterhood, in the form of Letitia 'Tish' Jones. Tish is well-known on the trail-running and adventure racing scene but was little heard of in the hard and fast world of club athletics. As the season progressed, most everyone that mattered knew enough to watch and learn.

Next up, we bounced from a bronze to a gold as we won a dramatic race at the SEAA cross-country relay. A gnarly trio of SA, Fee and Anne saw us home in a tense battle with London Heathside. Bouquets to Anne for stepping in at the last moment when it appeared we'd be a sandwich short of a picnic.

The following week saw a gung-ho quartet (make that five with Zoe's bump) take the long journey to Clumber Park, nr. Worksop for the relocated National 4 stage road relay. A tough nut to crack, but we made a good fist of it with our best return since 2005 and 4th best in our history - 17th. With the races coming thick and fast it was then a welcome return to the top flight of the Surrey League, where an excellent squad of ten rocketed straight in at number 2 in the charts. Tish easily took the win on debut (behind a guest), and the only wrinkle was that Thames grabbed a dangerous 51 point lead on us at the top.

We narrowly missed constructing a trio for a debut romp at the National cross-country relay - next year hopefully - and so were back in action at the South of the Thames 5m team race. More individual gold for Tish, while Jojo carded a splendid 6th to flag up her potential. Back to the Surrey League, and in an epic race at Nonsuch Park we were delighted to take the spoils. Tish outkicked Ruth Clifton and we packed beautifully to edge out a startling effort from W4, while Thames had to settle for 3rd. We were back in league contention.

We saw out a momentous 2012 with a repeat dose of bronze at the harsh environs of the South of the Thames Champs. A whopping six are needed to score, over 12k. But we managed it, despite losing two of our biggest guns in the days leading-up. But how heart-warming to see engine-roomers like Hester and Laura waltzing off into the sunset with hardware.

Round three of the Surrey League saw another incredibly hard-fought race as a mere 4 points separated the Belles, Herne Hill and Thames, with Dulwich out in front. We were 'only' 38 points off the top now, but we decided with several races clashing with the last fixture that we'd let the athletes choose the competition which best suited their needs on the day. Even if we'd cracked the whip, the league would still have remained just out of reach. This though meant we welcomed new faces into the squad, and ended up a laudable third in the league.

We had 14 strong ladies champing at the bit for the Southern Cross where we won a momentous bronze last year, and hoped for even better here. It was to our great chagrin that the race was cancelled due to the white stuff at vastly premature notice, and only three of the girls could make the rescheduled event, a week before the National. Still, we called up three super-subs, and placed a hard-fought 6th.

It was a long slog up to Sunderland for the National, and the race was a beast - freezing cold, deep mud and recent heavy snowfall. None of which bothered Tish who placed a momentous 17th. The rest fought so hard, and 6th place is easily the best in our history, and there's much potential to kick on from there. Onto the roads! Well, road, as the Southern 6 stage also got cancelled due to snow and ice - what a winter. But it meant the race became part of the National where we weren't quite at our merry best, but still ended up a mere 12 seconds off Southern bronze. 13th in 'the big one' was a tad short of expectation, such are our lofty ideals, but hardly shabby.

We are delighted to report however, that we are national champions at both the Half and full marathon. At Reading we boasted Tish, Sam and the welcome return of an old fave in Juliette Clark. Jules scored for us the last time we medalled in the National Half champs back in 2002, and here she was anchoring us home 11 years later. At the London Marathon our classic golden trio of last year: Sam, Fee and Lou were back for more, but this time all carrying niggles. Heroines they are, this only spurred them on, and 2012's cumulative 8:38:26 became 8:38:36 in 2013. Incredible consistency, and our title of 'Queens of the Marathon' carries over for another year.

So there it is, plenty of near misses, thrill, spills and what ifs, but four more entries to the club honours board, and every chance of more to come in 2013-14. Thanks and congrats to all who played their part. For in-depth detail and results is available in the relevant section on the website, but meanwhile:

item.title: Surrey County AA Road Relays, Wimbledon Park
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Setting Fire to the Rain

Will Cockerell reports: Ahhh, the Surrey road relay; as curtain raisers go it's a bit of a peach. A fizzy atmosphere; a unique, head-fry of a course; lots of familiar faces and a few new ones. Breakthrough runs a plenty, blinders from left field and clunkers from those who hoped for more. I made my Bels debut at this one 15 years ago and the enjoyment and anticipation remains just as it did in '98. Running is a simple sport: 'go hard or go home'. We are all lucky to have it in our lives and I'm sure I'm not the only one of the 360-odd souls here to be looking ahead to the next eight months with lip-smacking relish.

To the gun and with the rain easing off I had a crack at the opener for the first time since 2002, and was joined by Runa, who's in town to observe Anne's pursuit of the world ITU W45 title on Sunday. Around 4 mins into my run I observed Paskar nonchalantly on his way to the venue... our leg 2! Now that ups the stakes on my approach to 'cutting it fine'. 8th place pour moi was followed a minute late by a stellar run by Northern Lightning as she bashed out the fastest ladies' time of the day by 18 ticks, a fortnight shy of her 44th birthday. Pure class.

With a 90 second warm-up and 8-miles with the morning training group he leads in his legs, PO zoomed round to the day's second fastest, and took us into the lead, before scuttling off to work. A busy bee and our heartfelt thanks for stepping in for us at late notice. Meanwhile, the Belles were matching the men's fireworks as we purred over a sparkling debut by new signing Mel Wilkins. We set her a tricky target to garner selection for next week at Rushmoor and she marmalised it with a terrific sub-18 turn. Mel has only recently started taking her running seriously after a few years of dabbling, so hopefully at just 23 she is at the gateway to a strong career.

HBR set off with nearly a minute cushion over a girl who loves to chase, but is no longer Chase - Annette Gould. It's Hester's two year Belles anniversary and she has given us a dozen fine efforts in that time including some critical ones like securing us Div 1 Surrey League promotion and team bronze at the South of the Thames. Anyway, a fine battle was enjoyed by these two warriors and the lead was only surrendered as they entered the stadium.

The lads meanwhile saw a solid but reserved Knut get slightly mauled by a hungry pack of wolves before handing over to Roy who is stepping up his game in style. An excellent 15:52 catapults him to the very heart of our engine room, and if he keeps improving at the same rate, will soon be at the cutting edge of our affairs. Next up Trygve who defied expectations, and managed to see off a nasty cold (and his darling wife by 29 seconds), only finally bowing to the Herne Hill man late on.

Back to the Belles and Zoe waited a couple of minutes before pouncing on Vikki Filsell - who ably anchored the Senior Thames team to Surrey gold - but gave best to Mrs Smith in the Open race. That leggy stride maintains its metronomic efficiency from pre-Isaac and Evelyn days and there's every hope that Zoe is to now return to her form of 2009 and beyond.

So while the Belles sighed contentedly at a job well done, we could relax and await the arrival of 'one-foot-dry' Rob Norville. Just 5 ticks down on last year, Rob smoothly carried us round in 6th in the open race, and our season is underway with much to anticipate.

Left. Knowing that good steeplechasers always manage to keep one foot clear of the water, Robert heads for the shallow end after a less than perfect splash-down at a recent league match.

item.title: AFD Road Relays inc. SEAA Women's 4-Stage Championship
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Fighting to the Wire

Will Cockerell reports: The 2013-14 season continued in feel good fashion on Rushmoor's subtle slopes in a race of exceptional quality. Between 2008-2011, our time would have placed us 12th, 9th, 12th and 11th, but with the teams up to a record 69 starters, 18th was our lot here with a very new look team. The race was dominated by Aldershot's incredible squad, whose riches continue to grow. When the day's 3rd fastest athlete (and AFD's quickest), is unable to force her way into the A team, the other clubs can only murmur in approval. The 17th quickest of all the day's athletes frolicked down in their F team! We'll have her.

But enough about them, how are we? Well the squad is up to 37 now, more than double what it was four years ago. That 32 were elsewhere on this day is no problem. We made the decision to let Ms. Jones off the hook and go on a sub-34 minute roaring rampage of retribution in Swansea instead. So despite lower numbers this year, we still a talented team to parade.
It was a tad harsh to chuck Mel on first, but she was the one for the job after her stormer at Wimbledon. She got a nasty elbow boof in the midriff early doors, and was startled at the seething menace all around. But underneath a placid veneer, is someone who loves a scrap as much as the next girl. Top 30 was what we wanted, so 23rd was outstanding. The acorn continues to grow.
Thus Rose had far fewer to chase than we envisaged, and instead this purist 800 runner had to concentrate on holding steady, which she did in style, with a dazzling kick from 175 out. Enter stage left the debutante Zoe Doyle, stepping in for other Zoe who picked up a virus. The swap didn't cost us, as Z ran a blinder, just 2 ticks off Mel and our highest advancer of the day in the Open race (Vets included). What a find!

You know what you're gonna' get from Fee: no mistakes, no histrionics; just a clinical return. Feeling a little jaded after heavy marathon training, she advanced us some more and entering the arena treated us to a telling finish. With 600 to go she was under severe attack from Lucy Elliott who pinged a 2:06 for the 800 the other day (well, 1991), and AFD's Angel Collins 28 years Fee and L.E.'s junior. But at the final turn wonder-woman turned on the after-burners and left both floundering.
Many thanks to our quartet here for rallying to the cause and to reserve Hester who chose to be on stand-by instead of jetting off to Paris. Also thanks to the Club President for kindly registering the team, when his nerves couldn't take the match manager's delayed appearance at the venue any longer.

item.title: Aldershot F&D Relays, inc. SEAA 6-Stage Championship, Rushmoor Arena
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Claret & gold pyrotechnics

Alan Mead reports: With a few guys missing we were not going to be able to turn out a medal winning team so with the team manager suspecting that Nick Goolab was in good form, he took the decision to front load the six and showcase our colours. Having lit the blue touch-paper he then retired to a safe distance to watch the fireworks; and weren't they spectacular!

Nick simply ripped up the starting straight, disappearing from sight on the first loop, only to re-emerge a couple of minutes later with a 12 second lead. He’d torn the heart out of any opposition but the TM suddenly had a doubt in his mind … “I suppose he does remember that it’s two laps!” ‘Course he did, but it was quite staggering for all to behold a claret and gold vest going through at half way in an astounding 8:30 with a good half minute lead. The course record goes back years – to Brighton’s Andy Bristow with 17:07 – and has withstood runs from the likes of Mo Farah and Chris Thompson. Nick worked hard over that second 3k circuit but one could see from the occasional flicker of pain on his face that he had overdone it. Goodness alone knows what he would have run with a slightly steadier start. Nevertheless his 17:37 equalled Mark Miles’ club record from 2004 and he gave James Kelly a 28 second lead.

Knowing that it was going to be a front-loaded non-medal winning team, James had put in a hard old 20-miler the previous day as he works toward donning an England vest for the Toronto marathon. He was expecting to have company to take him around Rushmoor but here he was defending a mega-lead: “Thanks Nick!” But James is as strong as they come and not only did he defend the lead, he extended it to 34 seconds as Bedford dropped away and Thames Valley took up the chase.

A daunting task, then, for Craig Ruddy, making his Belgrave début? Not a bit of it; quite unfazed, our man who had just returned from a break in Turkey eased another few seconds away from the pack and we were 36 seconds to the good of an Aldershot squad that had supplanted the ‘Valley’.

Right in the firing line it was inevitable that Will Cockerell was going to be run down by the next AFD man and Bedford & County also squeezed into the frame but Will held it together to send Mike Trees away ahead of the Beagles’ John Beattie. How wonderful to see Mike, a day or two short of 51, battling it out with the youngsters; but the mêlée didn’t disturb his metronomic pace judgement as he was 9:55 for each circuit to run a time that would have put him top of the pile in the earlier M50 race. Wonderful running from our new M50 UK mile and 1500 metre record holder.

It was all up to Royston Maddams, then, stepping into the big time after a good run in the 'Surrey's'. It seemed that with luck we should finish 11th, 12th? Roy was having none of that though. A steady opening lap saw Kent, Highgate and Tonbridge come by and perhaps Brighton and one or two others moving up behind, but opening up his stride on the second tour of the arena the Belgrave rear-gunner wasn’t letting anyone else get on his tail and he brought us home a marvellous seventh.

Sometimes a non-medalling performance can be as pleasing as one that gets us on the podium. This was such a run. Nick’s time was fastest of the day by miles and he later admitted that while feeling the pain on that second circuit, he was driven on by the desire to show the running world that the Bels are alive and well after recent setbacks. Roll on the ‘National’.

Good to see James Browne back in a Belgrave vest after working abroad for years.

item.title: SEAA Men's 4x5k Cross-country Relay, Wormwood Scrubs
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Alan Mead writes:- Still struggling to get off the ground, this event hasn't yet attracted the number of entries in the senior age groups one would expect for an area championship but in the four times the race has been held Belgrave have supported it well and slowly the numbers rise.

Richard Ward dropped a bombshell before the race started: “Bad news Alan, I had to bin my lucky shorts this morning. They weren’t decent any longer!” As they had seen him through much of his career this was quite a blow – but we decided to soldier on as best we could.

Clapham Chaser Andy Maud ripped it up on stage 1, to set the day’s fastest, while the Cockerpillar got his legs turning over at a fair old speed to nudge inside 15 minutes for 12th; so it wasn’t quite 5k then! Holding on to Will for a good deal of the lap Sam Shore gave the B squad a handy start and as he handed over to Roy Maddams – and Roy’s on a meteoric upward trend at the moment and ran out of his socks – we had the unusual sight of the ‘B’s coming in one place down on the ‘A’s for whom Wardy was definitely out of s[h]orts. Four places fell to Paskar as he ran the fourth fastest time of the day and another three were dispatched by Mike Trees, the latter all set now for a crack at the World M50 5000m title in Brazil.

1 Bedford & County AC 57:54; 2 Newham & Essex Beagles 58:24; 3 Aldershot F& AC 59:36; … 5 Belgrave H 1:00:00; … 15 Belgrave H ‘B’ 1:04:40; … 34 teams started, 29 teams finished.

B team: S Shore (18) 16:16; R Maddams (13) 15:08; K Hegvold M50 (13) 16:08; R Norville (15) 17:08.

item.title: SEAA Women's 3x3.5k Cross-country Relay, Wormwood Scrubs
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Jodie adds eighth event to repertoire

Will Cockerell writes:- There was an uptick in attendance this year as the men saw finishing teams rise from 17 to 29, and the women from 10 to 16. Our ladies' win from last year has considerable value added now, as the TVH ladies blitzed it here for a fine return some 2:21 superior to what we managed in 2012. This is now a race that requires real attention, and is no longer: turn up and you should medal.

We kicked off with intriguing fare, with one of the finest athletes in the club for sure, but amongst her numerous outstanding talents, 3.5k over grassland is not necessarily one - yet! But a large unavailable list saw heptathlete Jodie Favell grab her chance and although it was 14 minutes of toil, she set Zoe up for a nice game of Space Invaders.

In just her second outing for the club, this extremely fit and able runner from Tring followed up on her fine Rushmoor debut with a brilliant display here, and reeled in no fewer than eight bodies for the sixth fastest of the day. Although there were quite a few more lined up for a returning skipper Sammi to chase, medals were always going to be an ask too far on this day, but with a time just 13 seconds down on last year, we can all breathe a huge sigh of relief that the surgeon's knife has made Amend.

item.title: ERRA National Men’s 6-Stage Road Relay, Sutton Coldfield
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Another epic relay run for the annals

Alan Mead reports: Another year and another page in the legend that tells of Belgrave’s participation in the ‘National’ Relays, a fable stretching back now over some 70 years. This last year has been one of drama one way or another and came so close to a fairy-tale ending on the hallowed ground of Sutton Coldfield. And talking of fairies – the tent fairies – down to just two in number now – had once again been in action as the first streaks of dawn smudged a lowering sky; and we’re so pleased that they had done their work to keep us mortals dry as a steady drizzle fell for most of the day.

A very good team had been lined up but had managed to remain under the radar as we moved in for the attack – and we were still under the radar as the first few legs unfolded. Steve Davies loves the cut and thrust of an opening leg – he has a 17:20 on this course – and a successful run out over a road mile in Spain the previous week told us that he is moving towards the sort of fitness that will see him in indoor action over the next few months; but nothing could be further from ‘indoors’ than nearly 6k of damp roadway in Sutton Park. We had hoped that the gap to the leaders would be not more than 45 seconds and in fact it was 55 so not too much to worry about then although there were rather more bodies for Craig Ruddy to chase than expected.

Didn't 'Ruds' chase

And didn’t ‘Ruds’ chase, in his first Sutton Park outing, clocking a fine 17:50 and picking up 14 men before having the task wrested away from him by Captain Paskar. Craig had vowed he would 'come on a bit' in the few weeks between the area race and this one and he was as good as his word. A controversial run by Central AC’s Robert Russell had taken the Scottish club eight seconds clear – controversial in that Russell normally runs in England for Thames Valley H (as does Ali Hay who turned out on leg 4). The rule book is a minefield but, hey! Let’s not go there.

Meanwhile the Lion of Nagongera (apologies for using this metaphor again – but we do like it!) was hungry for team success and vying throughout the third stage with Beagle Kevin Skinner. Up to 13th place, then, at halfway, perhaps half a dozen places behind our target and with Sale H Manchester a minute and twenty-four up the road.

Into the top ten

What a treat to see our course record holder (17:00) Phil Wicks in the Belgrave team again and ready to do whatever he could in spite of being just two weeks away from the Frankfurt Marathon. Phil had some largish gaps to bridge but at 17:27 he was fourth best on the stage and, importantly, none of those faster than him were up ahead. The Bels were now into the top ten, 27 seconds away from the medal positions.

Another on the brink of a marathon is James Kelly who fitted in a Sutton Park appearance as part of his journey from Spain to the Toronto Marathon next weekend when he’ll be racing for England. The puddles and damp conditions seemed to have held quite a few back time wise but Jim’s 17:51 indicates that he is pretty much at his fittest ever, only 7 seconds down on his best for this lap. This was really getting too exciting. In 5th spot now we were just 14 seconds away from bronze medals although still wanting 1:19 to get on terms with Sale who had set out to enjoy their fourth tour of the park in the lead, 52 seconds clear of second placed Tipton. “Have you got a strong finish?” ribbed a rival as he jogged past our tent. Have we? You bet!

The announcer started to wax lyrical

“Goolab!” went up the cry on the course as the runner in claret and gold was identified. Nick ripped round the dog-leg and up the hill, pulling back one, two and then three men. Even the announcer started to wax lyrical as he was made cognizant of the situation by spotters on the course and recalled over the public address system Nick’s past glories at National and European level. The gap to Sale was coming down. ‘Alty’s’ Mr Norman up the far end of the loop was heard to exclaim, “You know, he can do this!” But in fact it was just too big an ask. Nick had gone out at a pace that might have done it, could it have been maintained, but to chase down a prey that was out of sight for much of the lap is a tall order. Nevertheless, fourth fastest of the day – and that on the last stage with few bodies around him to pull on – was a tremendous achievement.

So, silver medals it was, 28 seconds adrift at the end, and to be honest everyone was pretty chuffed.

There had been some thought to putting Nick and Phil on stages three and five until finally the thought kicked in of maintaining our usual policy when we “have a chance”; always moving forward and never letting a position gained ever be lost again throughout the race. Would it have worked differently? Who knows? One can’t help thinking that such a solid Sale crew would always have had a half minute advantage whatever we did.

item.title: ERRA National Women's 4-Stage Road Relay, Sutton Park, Sutton Coldfield
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Naughty But Nice

Will Cockerell writes: As in 2011 we fielded two strong teams for this most competitive of events. Our B's had the tough option of bettering their counterparts of two years ago who were littered with bandits, boxing above their weight. Well, the 2013 vintage took a deep breath and went 3 seconds faster; oh, and they've improved from the 7th best B team in the land, to 6th. Many thanks to you all, so much more fun to have you there. Co-skipper Jojo went 15-20 secs better than expected, Fee was back to her best after a tricky last few weeks, and ran-over 11 girls on two; Vicki was there as always, to keep us in check; and Fi Maddocks made her relay debut in style with a fine finishing burst.

A few minutes up the road and our A-squad did it the hard way after we started with our ace... how very not to behave in public! But, ooooh sometimes it's fun to be just a little naughty. Our men's TM had a similar swish outside the off-stump down in Rushmoor, and weren't the crowd treated to one of the most exciting pieces of athletics since the last lap of the Munich 5,000 of '72. Well, this was pretty special too. After we programmed 14:20 into the little computer in Tish's back [designed in Japan, engineered in Germany], she beat the mark by 1 tick and had a splendid duel with doyennes Lily Partridge and Juliet Potter, both of whom have been winning medals on the national club scene for a decade plus. One recalls Lily as a U13 shrub convalescing in our club tent after she won team gold at the 2004 National cross. Great running then, for a time that would stand up as 6th best of the day.

Welcome back to the big time Sammi Amend. It's always a close call to chuck an athlete recuperating from an 'op' into the den of iniquity that is Stage 2 of a relay, but SA more than justified her selection, in what must have been like running in a tumble-dryer. Another slightly gung-ho selection with the calibre of Fee thrashing away in the B's, was Mel, but her two excellent runs in the Surreys and Southerns warranted her place. This was a real step-up in class, and she scrapped like a cornered tiger. Well done Mel - take the standard of running you saw here and let it inspire you in your training. And then our enforcer Lou, barrelling on, refusing to get caught by the flying Squires of Hallamshire, and nearly running down Tipton. All eyes on April then, when our strength in depth will be telling.

item.title: 2XU Men's Surrey Cross Country League Division 1, Race 1, Wimbledon Common
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
New faces in the scoring ten

There were plenty of new faces to be seen in our team for the opening Surrey League fixture. Many of Charlie Dickinson’s Battersea squad turned out and of these, making a big impact in our scoring ten, was Sam Village, getting in among the old hands Roy Maddams and Matt Taylor. Matt Welsh, also a ‘Charlie’s Runner’ likewise made the scoring ten in his first outing.

There’s no doubting that Roy is upping his game, targeting the Cockerpillar at every outing and with a self-confessed mission of making our 12-Stage team by next spring. He celebrated his highest league place with an après run extra lump of chocolate cake but will no doubt wear that off at his next training session with our Maidenhead training group that includes Mike Trees, Pete Willis, John Needham, etc.

US runner Kyle Marks led in our scorers and will be a great asset in the races to come this winter. Also back to the old routine was James Browne after years of working overseas.

Kent AC seemed to have the team event stitched up with plenty of forward placings, but Thames came back at them towards the back end of each club’s scoring squads. With plenty of our own runners unavailable for this race we had to be pretty pleased with an opening 4th team spot.

Three youngsters lined up in the biggest Young Athletes field we’ve seen in a while and Zayd Addicott caught the eye, finishing 27th in the 58 strong field with only four lads in his own age group ahead of him.

The event was a joint fixture promoted by Belgrave H and Hercules Wimbledon AC and all seemed to run smoothly; many thanks to all those who helped.

item.title: Women's Surrey Cross Country League, Division 1, Match 1, Lightwater
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Lurgy, M25 and a Dreadful Baton Exchange Can't Fell Belles

Will Cockerell writes:-

[Indy and his father have boarded the airship]
Indiana Jones: 'Well, we made it!'
Professor Henry Jones: [looking out from behind his newspaper] 'When we are airborne, with Germany behind us, then I will share that sentiment!'

Well, we shared Indy's view three days before this season opener as a superb squad was assembled... but we'd have done well to be more cautious, as we then lost eight strong runners - five to illness, two to niggles, one on a break... Hang on, we were suddenly running out of ideas!

But not to worry. Fee has never missed a Surrey League in over two years with us, Tish was ever-game, and Zoe D has quickly become one of our 'bankers'. Add to that Jojo and new kid 'KeriMac', and we still had the quintessential quintet. Our sweepers were no slouches in Rose, Hester and Jodie.

To the start and no Jodie. It was noted that the gun came at 11:58 and 19 seconds. I do dislike it when starters do this. Runners are an idiosyncratic bunch and pre-race rituals are often planned to the second. Several runners were caught on the hop, and poor Jodie arrived plum on 12, but the field was two minutes away. The M25 had not been kind to her, but off she chased like a trooper. After the small 1k loop she was already catching runners, and now for the excruciating hilarity of our match manager Chas attempting to pass over her number. But the gap between paw and outstretched number was half a yard, and there it remained for 40 yards. One had visions of this wretched scene continuing for 400 yards, or even 4000. Jodie Favell slows down for nobody. Charlie dug deep and found a turn of speed he hadn't called upon in years and the exchange was finally complete.

There was nearly as much excitement up at the front as three tremendous runners in Cathy Ansell, T.A.J. and Bleasdale J, got acquainted. However, on the long descent toward the middle of the race, Jules decided to step it up, and showed that her training is moving in the right direction after a quiet year; this her first race since a 33:53 in Dublin six months ago. A gap of 25 seconds opened quite quickly, but Tish kept plugging away and kept things to under a minute by the close, whilst opening a 51 second gap on Ansell and 1:46 to fourth, Fi Clark, who won this fixture four times between 2008-2011.

A little further back was the splendid sight of Zoe and Fee having a ding-dong-battle-royale some half-dozen spots higher than expected. Fee is finding a real sharpness in her legs, as she focuses a little more on speed in her training. Best of luck in Frankfurt on Sunday. As for Zoe, three Belles outings and all zingers, what a find.

Right, who to settle the account? The ever-reliable co-skipper of course who turned an ankle just before the start, and toiled for much of the race, before finding hidden reserves and blasting through the field in the last 2k. And just ahead of her, another outstanding new find in Keri Mackenzie. It's the second Scot we've picked up this summer, and if Rowena runs with Keri's determination and talent, our message to both will be, "you'll do!"

Rose whackily led out the field for the first 250 which was fun to observe, while HBR kept it as solid as ever, and Jodie placed over 100 bodies behind her in the combined race. This all adds up to a fine opening league win; the first time we've done that since 2006 when the Iron Lady, Ms. Wellington, led us home. The margin over 2nd and 3rd is 49 and 52. A buffer yes, but "We made it?!" Not yet, Indy, not yet.

Eleven year-old Yasmin Marghini came up against some tough opposition in the under 13 race but did well to place 10th in a field that was 63 strong. Look for her to be among the first three in time to come.

item.title: ECCA Men's National Cross Country Relay Championship, Berry Hill Park, Mansfield
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Claret & gold remains prominent at national level

Alan Mead reports: The drama began early when a phone call to Paskar, not yet present just before the train was about to leave St Pancras, revealed that he was just getting out of the shower – at home in Roehampton – thinking the race was on Sunday. Following swiftly given instructions he donned his kit, leaped onto his bike and pedalled furiously to Putney where he locked his steed and then rode the tubes, East Midlands Trains and taxi, arriving 45 minutes before he was due to race. While the latter stages of this entertainment was going on the remainder of our quartet warmed up confident of a top six place and maybe a shot at the medals.

The start had been moved yet again in the evolution of this course and we now believe the race distance to be somewhere around 30 seconds per stage longer than when we set the course record in 2003. As the gun fired and the first stagers of 184 teams climbed towards the top of the first loop a claret streak shot from the pack as if fired from a cross bow and with not a minute gone Nick Goolab had thrown down a challenge that was to be totally ignored. Ripping around the first 2.5k circuit he was 10 seconds clear of the pack and it stretched to 12 before the race to the line pulled him back a couple of ticks. It was a great run from Nick that stood up as second best of the day.

We all knew that Mark Pollard would be in the firing line after our expected strong start and he had the most unenviable task of all – hanging on as best he could while under attack. Andi Jones of Stockport slowly pulled him back but the real turbulence was just a little bit further down where Aldershot’s Andy Vernon was creating havoc, moving up from 18th, to 10th to 3rd and dragging a whole flurry of runners with him as he progressed. His second circuit saw him inevitably surge into a lead which AFD were not to lose – and in Vernon’s wake Polly found himself mugged by Sale, Bristol & West, Sale, Bedford, Luton and Shaftesbury Barnet.

An unshaven Paskar, showing no other signs of his hasty flight from London, was soon running smoothly and overhauled the latter two clubs but those left ahead were all serious contenders for medals and it was going to take something extraordinary now to make further advancement. Kris Gauson was keen to take on the anchor role, having flown round the course at Cumbernauld the previous week in the Scottish relay. He flew past runner after runner, but they were all lapped men and although the gap came down to those ahead we couldn’t gain any more positions.

As it happened, Bristol & West had fallen foul of the entry rules and we were thus promoted from 6th to 5th. So, excellent running from our men and claret & gold remains prominent in the big races.

item.title: ECCA Women's National Cross Country Relay Championship, Berry Hill Park, Mansfield
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Belles create history at Mansfield

Charlie Dickinson writes: It was the first time in the history of this prestigious event, the National Cross Country relay, that Belgrave had sent a women’s team. In the past they had preferred the easier journey to take part in the Reigate Priory event rather than the long haul up to Mansfield.

Our three heroines, Rose, Jojo and Fiona (a very late replacement for the virus stricken Mel) all ran really well over the fast, but by no means easy, 3km lap. On arrival, we were welcomed to a very nasty squall, soaking us in our warm up and sending some of the tents high into the air. Luckily, the rained ceased in time for the start of the race, but left the open fields very wet. This with the winding, undulating part of the course through the woods makes for quite a tricky circuit.

On the first leg, Rose coped well with the elbows and knees on the first corner and ran a very sensible controlled race. Coming out of the woods, she dug deep to get round that nasty extra loop up around the top of the park and finished with her usual flourish. Anything around 12 minutes would have been good on the course, Rose ran 11.39.

On leg two, Jojo set off purposefully to try to wind some of the other teams in. She did this in a very controlled manner pulling us up several places. The question was, who would be quicker, Rose with her extra speed or Jojo with her superior stamina? The pair had trained stride for stride in the sessions leading up to the race, and therefore not surprisingly, there were only a couple of seconds in it with Jojo clocking 11.37.

Our real star was Fiona, giving up a hockey match at very short notice to make up the team. Fiona is very strong as she had shown only two weeks previously running 3.38 for the Yorkshire marathon off very little training. She held the Belle’s position on the last leg finishing just a second behind MK who were in 32nd place out of well over 100 teams.

As we were unable to register Fiona at such short notice, we had to, unfortunately, run as a non-scoring team. However, we have now created a precedent and hopefully this will become a regular event in the Belle’s racing calendar.

item.title: South of the Thames 5 Miles Team Race, Streatham Common
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Gold medals for the Belles and Paskar

A magnificent triumph for the Belles on what must be one of the toughest cross country courses anywhere, writes Charlie Dickinson. Our scoring four won by the huge margin of 26 points with Keri Mackenzie winning the individual bronze medal. They were supported by real gutsy runs from Zoe Smith, who battled round in spite of sleepless nights over the last week with her baby, then Helen and Jen racing each other all the way round on their debuts for the Belles.

Many of us knew the open part of Streatham Common, we had done hill reps there for many years, but we had never ventured past the car park into the wooded, muddy and very hilly Norwood Grove. this part of the course was brutal! Our team were led off cautiously by Fee and Zoe Doyle on the downhill start which was very soon channelled into a narrow path. Things settled down along the flat part of the course, parallel with the A23, about the only flat part! Then up the long drag against a bitter north easterly wind. It was here on the first lap that Keri started to pull through the field passing both Fee and Zoe although all three were packing nicely. Then came Felicity, back with the Belles after a couple of years just doing Triathlons working brilliantly to stay in touch with the other three. Had she gone off to fast, would she die on this course?

Keri continued to move through the field on the second and third laps up to fourth and edging closer to the medals. Then Zoe and Fee, within sight of each other showing their incredible strength and maintaining their positions. So did Felicity, she just hung on, not losing ground, a wonderful, tough performance. At the end, Keri only just failed to catch the South London girl in third place, but it didn't matter, the winner, Fiona Clarke from Reigate was a non scorer so Keri deservedly got the bronze medal. With Zoe 6th just edging out a THH girl on the line, Fee 8th and Felicity 12th our scoring four won the Norah Heathfield shield for the very first time. A great performance by those four backed up by Zoe Smith, Helen and Jen.

Incidentally, adds Alan Mead, that winning trophy was given to the South of Thames by our own late Jim Heathfield, Treasurer of the Association for 21 years, in memory of his sister. It was the first time that Belgrave have won it.

And what of the men? Paskar was determined to avenge recent defeats by Kent AC men, including Johnny Gilbert, and together with Rogers of Aldershot they broke away on the first lap with the Kent man mostly making the running. Paskar started to get a bit frisky on the second circuit and by the third time round the Common he'd prised open a lead which he maintained until he crossed the line and waited to warmly greet Gilbert at the end of what had been a fierce struggle.

It was so nice to see Roy Maddams back in the team. Running to work a few weeks back he had a blackout and had no further knowledge of what was going on until he woke up in hospital with a fractured jaw and other damage to the Maddams phizog. Tests have revealed no underlying serious problems and to come back and duff up Will after a few weeks of very little running was a great achievement. 'Cockers' wasn't taking it lying down though. A quickly improving James Browne gave both of them something to think about early on and although Will managed to pull him back here was nothing he could do about Roy who was fully aware that he must keep the pressure up to stay ahead of the man who had been his target since the beginning of the season.

item.title: Women's Surrey Cross Country League, Division 1, Match 2, Coulsdon
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Belles Navigate A Bunch of Cows

From quiet beginnings this term, the train has built up speed and is now a runaway train; and the great news, with three big wins in the locales of Leeds, Streatham and Coulsdon, is that the brakes are in no danger of being fixed. Missing as many as ten top-guns here, including talisman Tish, meant that our 'midfield' cranked into gear and didn't they just love the adrenaline rush that comes with responsibility. The Downs were at their kindest considering how treacherous they've been in recent years and once half-a-dozen cows had been politely finessed from their powwow plumb on the racing line, all was set for 313 of Surrey's finest to hot-step it on the dance floor.

Our lines were led by find of the year Zoe Doyle (left), a softly-spoken mother of three who doesn't appear too alarming a prospect from a distance, though at close quarters her razor-sharp calves give a clue. Superb stuff from ZD as her Lightwater 12th was sliced in half. Mel (right) was a wee bit gutted after a sub-par return at Leeds, but she put in the hard yards in Egypt of all places, and returned fit as a flea. Magnificent stuff, and matched for excellence of run by the skipper who led out the gang early doors. JJR settled down, but not by much with a stellar 14th, up from 21st on match 1.

Wonderful to see Flic Cole back in business regularly for the Belles. She spoilt us in March 2011 with a coupla' gems, but was elsewhere till last month. She hung in great here and saw off the ever game Fee who was only 3% to start on Friday with various niggles, but her unbroken Surrey League sequence now stretches to over two years. Only eight Belles have had more scoring runs since 1990 than the Vixster and she flew along (before continuing her diary with her sister's wedding); and with HBR nearly a minute up on Lightwater and hockey star Helen dispatching over 150 bods, our work was done.

Herne Hill and Thames upped their games and we are not safe yet from a violent assault from our stripy friends. But our lead has stretched to 76 points and with Dulwich having a bit of a 'mare, at least we've isolated the enemy. Now to apply the anaesthetic.

In the U13 race an excellent run from Adelaide Clair who finished 10th in 18.58, winner Elsa Palmer DMV 10.05. Unfortunately, Yasmin Marghini had to drop out with a pulled hamstring after being well placed.

It was nice to see the two sisters, Marie and Juliette Michot also running even though they just missed the start. Marie is 11 and Juliette only 9 but they both completed the tough course very well.

item.title: Women's South of the Thames CC Championship, Wimbledon Common
item.dc:creator: belgravearchive
item.content:encoded:
Brilliant Belles Blitz The Field - Paskar Retains His Title

Co-captain Jojo Rhodes reports: A strong team of ladies lined up on a rainy and overcast Winter Solstice day, hopeful of building on the team victory in the South of Thames 5 miles last month. The course sounded straightforward: three equal laps following the paths of Wimbledon Common with the famous climb to the windmill to savour; but the rain and mud made the going tough. As the runners came through the start/finish to complete lap one it was clear the Belles were taking the conditions in their stride and very much in pole position, ably led by Sammi – co-captain and star marathon runner.

Drama at the close of the second lap, – a runaway horse no less! scattering runners to right and left. Fortunately it veered onto another path away from the action with no damage done except for a degree of collective anxiety amongst the nearby spectators. Sam was still running strongly and heading for the top three, followed by the fearsome duo of Mel and Zoe D, focused on the job in hand. Next up was Keri, nursing a sore knee but determinedly battling on. Chasing hard was Zoe S, looking serene over the mud. Hester, another marathon specialist, looked at home and she was closely followed by debutante Abbie.

A great final lap from Sammi meant she was rewarded with a silver medal. Despite a professed dislike of cross-country it was a superb performance. Mel and Zoe D posted 6th and 7th, and rounding the final corner Mel had enough in hand to give a big smile and just three seconds behind yet another assured run from Zoe. So 3 in the top 7, three more needed...

Keri came in 15th gritting her teeth through the pain, and Zoe S, on low weekly mileage, finished 22nd - so much more to come from her anon. Hester performed her duties of sixth scorer with distinction, followed in 31st by Abbie – we look forward to many more Belles outings from her! Some quick mathematics from Charlie showed a resounding team victory, and all the signs are good for the Belles looking ahead to the New Year.

And while all this was going on Paskar Owor was majestic. A bunch of Kentish men surrounded him early on - Dartford, Tonbridge and Kent AC colours all being prominent - but soon it was just Johnny Gilbert and our man knocking six bells out of each other. By the start of the final lap Paskar had gained a dozen metres and appeared supremely confident while Gilbert looked as if he could no longer retaliate; and so it proved. Team medals were blown away when we lost three or four men before the race through heavy colds and a couple more through injury; but it was a successful day as this home promotion went without a hitch and the start/finish crew even managed to spend 30 minutes in The Fox & Grapes before the start.

Merry Christmas Everyone!
